title: the star: creative essence as a regenerative giving
content:
this is tarot work guides — in which I contemplate one card a week as an intuitive guide for my creative business practice.

guiding question for the star

what would it look like to give to your work from a place of your deepest creative life essence — while trusting in its replenishing, regenerative nature? how would your relationship to your work — and to yourself — change?

*

I pulled The Star on the week in which I birthed a big milestone — otherworldly, my web alchemy studio, which reflects a decade of my journey integrating art and business. in my work journal, I wrote down that “otherworldly feels like The Star” — not just because the website is filled with cosmic motifs, but because it represents a carefully defined business container and creative channel through which I can give from my true essence — to the right projects and clients — while feeling replenished in doing so. this feeling of alignment is so much harder than it sounds. for me, accessing The Star required a clarity born from discernment; that is, learned from years and years of doing the wrong projects, working with the wrong clients, and doubting my creative worth.

divine nature of being

The Star never, ever doubts her creative worth.

self-doubt never even occurs to her, probably because The Star knows that she is made up of divine essence — the raw material of universes. she is absent of all the self-consciousness and neuroses of humans, and the idea of “trusting yourself” doesn’t even make sense to The Star, probably because there is no separate “self” to trust. she is already one with all that is around her — she is a part of life source, itself.

thus, the Star is a card about a particular kind of giving — giving from an essence which has been divinely received, giving as an act of channeling. whatever gifts the Star has to give, she didn’t earn them through hard work. she didn’t deserve them. she simply pours forth what she has received from the cosmos — by simply being herself.

giving from comes from being — not from working, or earning, or proving worthiness.

giving is a part of her essential, naked nature; it’s an expression of freedom, generosity, and surrender. this is not a measured giving; there is a sense of infinite abundance and replenishment in it. she pours her essence to both earth and the pool; her body touches both land and water. the Star arrives after the disruptive shock of the Tower, and represents a glowing sense of hope and renewal.

lessons and practices from the star

when I asked myself what “being the Star” in my creative life and business might look and feel like, I thought about it in 3 parts, which I’ll share, first, as questions.

  1. BEING — divine creative essence — what does it feel like to “be” in your divine creative essence — that place where you can give from your true nature? can you sense and feel it in your body? where does that presence live? what does it feel like?

  2. GIVING — as replenishment — what kind of giving feels replenishing and regenerative — such that the more you give, the more you feel nourished? can you distinguish between work that is generative vs. depleting? I write about this idea of re-generative energy in business here.

  3. CONTAINERS — earth and water — what, in your creative or business world, represents your metaphorical earth & water — as clear containers for your giving? this could be any part of your creative or business ecosystem.

the practice of being The Star means committing to your truth/purpose/natural gifts — the work which you do naturally, the work which feeds your soul — because that’s the kind of work that replenishes your energy. when you do that work, you’re able to give from a place of infinite resourcedness — to the containers of the larger earthly body/ecosystem/community that holds you — and then, that feeds back into your divine essence.

perhaps a very reductive, 101 version of this might look like this —

  1. find the work that feels like your “gift”

  2. keep giving to it — but in a way that truly nourishes you

  3. define the right containers — that nourish yourself AND expand to others


in meditating on this card, I’ve realized that my practices around building digital ecosystems and worlds — over using platforms like social media — are very Star-like in their generative, contained essence.

all energy is sacred. no energy is wasted.

giving as regeneration

what’s essential to this cycle of giving is that your giving must feel like receiving. giving from Star energy feels like replenishment. you receive the gift from a divine source — and your act of channeling that gift feeds you, and the landscape around you. there is no conception of scarcity in a self-regenerating ecosystem. there is no competition, or pressure, or fighting to be seen or heard.

in practical terms, this might mean being more deliberate about containers and channels — HOW and WHERE you give. does posting on social media feel replenishing, or depleting? does forcing yourself to time block your day energize you, or deplete you? how can you restructure the ways in which you create and share your work — so that it feels as easeful as possible?

if anything, this idea of regenerative giving is entirely in opposition to the notion of “the starving artist” — that narrative in which the more you give to your art, the more your material life feels undernourished. the “starving artist” operates from a mode of separateness — MY art vs. the world, whereas The Star calls for deep integration: I am of the world, and the world is of me. this is about finding a deep alignment and integration — within yourself — of all the constellations of meaning, purpose, and beauty.

for me, my Star Practice consists of channeling my creative energy into my websites — as infinite creative vessels, living ecosystems, and digital worlds. it’s meant embracing myself as an artist-entrepreneur, where my creative energy IS my greatest business resource. I pour that abundant life energy — my inspirations, art, ideas, contemplations, and visions — like cosmic seeds. then, I watch them sprout and grow.
